newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Clinton telephones Netanyahu on summit.
newsitem.headline: Clinton telephones Netanyahu on summit.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton telephoned Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday and said he hoped an Arab-Israeli summit in Washington would halt violence and advance peace moves, Netanyahu's spokesman said.

"During the 20-minute conversation, the prime minister thanked the president for his invitation to the Washington summit and expressed his appreciation for the president's attempts to help move the peace process forward," he said.
"The president said the results required of the summit in Washington are a stop to the violence and the early resumption of negotiations on outstanding issues," the spokesman said.

Netanyahu, he added, agreed with Clinton's comments and said that for Israel the aim of the summit would be to ensure the region calms down and peace talks are renewed between Israel and the Palestinians.

Clinton also telephoned Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to invite him to the White House meeting. A PLO official said Arafat first wanted to persuade Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak to attend and would go to Cairo on Monday.

Palestinian-Israeli clashes since Israel opened a Jerusalem tunnel near Moslem holy sites last Tuesday have claimed the lives of 69 people. It was the worst such violence since the signing of a landmark Israel-PLO peace deal three years ago.
